newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ top 40 share index rallies to new record.
newsitem.headline: NZ top 40 share index rallies to new record.

text.p: New Zealand's top 40 share index rallied 0.9 percent on Thursday to its highest point since starting in 1991.
By 1.15 p.m. (0115 GMT) the NZSE40 Capital Index was up 19.96 points at 2,513.12 having earlier struck an all-time peak of 2,514.98.
The market largely withstood the latest missive from central bank governor Don Brash, who said monetary conditions had eased too far.
Brash reiterated that desired monetary conditions had not changed since the release of the Reserve Bank's Monetary Policy Statement last Friday -- 825 on the bank's Monetary Conditions Index.

"Against this background, actual monetary conditions have been too easy over recent days. We will be looking to see actual conditions settle closer to the announced desired levels", Brash said in a statement.
Telecom was the main driver of the share market, gaining 16 cents to NZ$7.70.
Most other leaders posted only minor gains, but Lion Nathan was also very strong, rising five to $3.80.
